audit.why: EVEN at 6/10 with 52.51% over 577 games holds up, and the mirror left the equivalent rating alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 disagreed with the mirror or with their own whys — level 2 and 3 were marked Tryndamere above whys calling them even, and level 4-5 was Skill above a why saying Maokai wins it.
audit.why: The mirror set row 0 to Tryndamere and rows 2, 3 and 4-5 to Maokai, with first item Skill. Levels 2-5 are his because Twisted Advance is untargetable on the way in and roots on arrival, and Bramble Smash pushes you off him every 7 seconds.
audit.corrected: Rows flipped in matched pairs with ratings adjusted, and whys 2, 3, 5 and 6 rewritten to agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page's headline instruction was 'His lock-on root. E-spin out of it.' — advice you cannot follow.
audit.why: Twisted Advance roots on arrival, and a rooted Tryndamere cannot cast Spinning Slash at all; the spin has to happen before it lands. Worse, he is untargetable for the whole dash, so any crit or auto aimed at him during it is wasted. Real numbers: W 14/13/12/11/10 at 525, Bramble Smash 7/6.5/6/5.5/5 at 600, Sapling Toss 18/17/16/15/14 at 1100 and stronger in brush, Nature's Grasp 130/110/90 at 3000.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d, report[5], breakdown.cooldowns, spikes[0], mid and four phase whys rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nature's Grasp was never described as a retreat-cutter, and Sap Magic's refresh condition was absent.
audit.why: The ultimate is a 3000-range advancing wall that roots, so it takes your exit rather than your health — and you have no dash to cross it. Sap Magic heals him on a cooldown that shortens each time he casts a spell, which is what makes Grievous Wounds matter in a long trade.
audit.corrected: Added to late, phases[0].why, phases[5].why and spikes[2].

edits.before: Spin up fury on the wave before contesting anything. Identify how Maokai contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Spin up fury on the wave. Sap Magic heals him on a cooldown that shortens every time he casts, so deny him the free casts.

edits.before: E lets you spin in and out of exchanges on your terms. Only take the trade when Maokai's Twisted Advance is down.
edits.after: Twisted Advance makes him untargetable for the dash and roots on arrival — your crits whiff during it, so back out early.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Maokai must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Bramble Smash knocks you back every 7s and Sapling Toss zones from 1100. He owns the ground between you and the wave.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Twisted Advance's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: His root into sapling poke is the all-in, and Twisted Advance is 14s at rank 1 — that gap is the only safe window you get here.

edits.before: Stridebreaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Twisted Advance's cooldown.
edits.after: Stridebreaker helps you stick, but Sap Magic heals the chip back — bring Grievous Wounds.

edits.before: Level 2 is even as his Twisted Advance root comes online and threatens a punish.
edits.after: Level 2 is his: Twisted Advance is untargetable on the way in and roots on arrival.

edits.before: Level 3 stays a skill window between his W-E root poke and your trade discipline.
edits.after: Level 3 is his: Bramble Smash knocks you off him every 7 seconds at rank 1.

edits.before: Level 6 flips to you: R Undying Rage negates his root-setup all-in and heals you back up.
edits.after: Level 6 is even: Undying Rage answers his root all-in, but Nature's Grasp cuts your exit.

edits.before: With lifesteal your Q sustain out-heals his sapling poke and you run him down.
edits.after: First item is even: Sap Magic heals the chip back unless you buy anti-heal.

edits.before: - Maokai Twisted Advance: matchup-defining — His lock-on root. E-spin out of it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Twisted Advance: 14s at rank 1, 525 range — he is untargetable on the way in, so your crits whiff. - Bramble Smash: a 7s knockback. - Nature's Grasp: a 130s wall that roots — save Flash for the terrain.

edits.before: Track Maokai's Twisted Advance (Root): His lock-on root. E-spin out of it. When it is down — Crit him down.
edits.after: Twisted Advance is untargetable while it travels — your autos whiff, so leave before it lands, not after.

edits.before: His lock-on root. E-spin out of it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: It roots on arrival, so spin out before it lands — afterwards you cannot.

edits.before: That is Maokai's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Rooted, you cannot Spinning Slash out — the root is the trade, not his damage.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Saplings hit harder in brush; take the open path around them.

edits.before: Maokai's Twisted Advance (W) root into Sapling Toss (E) poke is his kill setup; stay out of his saplings in brush and don't get W-rooted next to his jungler.
edits.after: Twisted Advance goes untargetable on the way in and roots on arrival into sapling poke; nothing you throw lands during it, and saplings hit harder in brush.

edits.before: With lifesteal your Q sustain out-heals his sapling poke; run him down whenever his W root is on cooldown since it's his only lock-down.
edits.after: Sap Magic heals him off his own casts, so Grievous Wounds decides the long trade; run him down in the 14 seconds Twisted Advance is on cooldown.

edits.before: Levels 2-5 are a skill window centred on his Twisted Advance (W) root — if he catches you with W into Sapling Toss (E) poke, especially with jungle nearby, the trade goes badly. Level 4 is his clearest window; respect the root, dodge saplings, and hold Spinning Slash (E) as your out until 6.
edits.after: Levels 2-5 are his, centred on Twisted Advance — he is untargetable while it travels and roots on arrival, so a crit thrown at the dash is wasted. Level 4 is his clearest window with jungle nearby; respect the root, walk around saplings, and hold Spinning Slash as your out until 6.

edits.before: From level 6 you take over: R Undying Rage nullifies his all-in and a first-item lifesteal spike lets your Q out-sustain his poke. Run him down when his W is on cooldown and split the sidelane — he's a peel tank with no answer to a fed diver.
edits.after: From level 6 you take over: Undying Rage answers his all-in and lifesteal funds the run-down. Keep Flash for Nature's Grasp — a 3000-range wall that roots is how he cuts your exit, not his damage. Split the sidelane; he cannot duel you.

notes: The packet's suspectName on wants.foe[0] is a false positive: Twisted Advance is the correct Riot name. The page's core instruction, repeated in dosFull, report[5] and breakdown.cooldowns, was to spin out of his root — you cannot cast Spinning Slash while rooted, so that advice fails at the exact moment it is needed. The kit file tags Bramble Smash with grounding and Riot's text does not mention it; I left grounding out. As in the mirror, I did not restate the unverified 'unkillable for 5 seconds' figure or the claim that crits reduce Spinning Slash's cooldown.
